# ADR-0002: Every file under modules/ is a flake-parts module loaded by import-tree, and flake.nix is generated by flake-file

Status: accepted
Date: 2026-05-31
Backfilled: 2026-11-03, from `porting.md` (top sections), `overview.md`, commit `8289b87`,
and ank's account of the switch.

## Context
v1 (the `v1` branch, archived in `old_modules/`) was a conventional flake that already
used `flake-parts.lib.mkFlake`, but everything was wired by hand: the `imports` list in
`flake.nix`, index files such as `modules/nixos/default.nix` and `machines/registry.nix`,
`inputs`/`outputs` threaded into each file as arguments, and every input declared in one
hand-kept `flake.nix`. v1 had 73 relative-path imports. Adding a module meant editing the
module, an index file and sometimes `flake.nix`, and keeping that plumbing straight was
the main cost of every change.

Once the repo was on flake-parts, the dendritic pattern was the natural next step: if
every file is a flake-parts module, the wiring disappears. No other layout was seriously
considered.

## Decision
- Every `.nix` file under `modules/` is a top-level flake-parts module, imported
  automatically by import-tree (`modules/dendritic.nix`). There are no file-based
  imports between modules; they reach each other through `self.*` and `config.flake.*`.
- File and directory names carry no meaning; only what a file declares does. A `_`
  prefix keeps a file or directory out of import-tree (shared snippets, data, parked
  modules).
- `flake.nix` is generated by flake-file. Inputs are declared next to the code that uses
  them (`flake-file.inputs.<name>`), and `nix run .#write-flake` regenerates the file.

## Consequences
- Adding a module is adding a file. Outside kalam's nixvim configuration, `modules/`
  has 2 relative-path imports.
- Every `.nix` file is evaluated as a module, so data files and non-module Nix
  (an agenix rules file, helper attrsets) must sit under a `_` path or the flake breaks.
- Flakes skip untracked files: a new file is invisible to evaluation until it is
  `git add`ed (`git add -N` is enough).
- A module that declares a new input and imports from it can't be written in one step,
  because `write-flake` evaluates the flake (see the terranix M1 entry in `porting.md`).
- Non-standard outputs written from many files need a declared type to merge, which is
  what ADR-0003 is about.
